summary: Specifies the S Hexdump Format, an XML-based open format for describing binary data in hexadecimal notation. It can handle both small and large dumps and is neutral about transport and vendor. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Computers write binary data as strings of letters and numbers. This memo gives a tidy, labeled way to write such strings so any program can read them.

questions: what is the s hexdump format
subtitle: An XML format for writing binary data as labeled hexadecimal blocks, with a SHA-1 check on each block.

tldr.problem: Older hex dump formats such as S-records are not truly open or well defined, cannot describe very large data sizes or mixed word sizes, and use checksums too weak to catch errors reliably.
tldr.mechanism: SHF wraps hexadecimal data in a small XML structure: one dump element holding one or more block elements. Each block carries its address, word size, length and a 20-byte SHA-1 digest of the data it represents.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard with its own media type, application/shf+xml. It describes a dump only, and it does not protect the file as a whole.

today: RFC 4194 is a Proposed Standard from October 2005. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a New Hex Dump Format
sections.content:
People in computing, networking and embedded systems use several formats for hexadecimal data. A common one is the S-record, which reportedly originated at Motorola; the S Hexdump Format (SHF) is named in its honour. Typical uses are firmware, flash memory images, FPGA bitstreams, graphics resources and routing tables.

The RFC complains that none of the old formats are truly open, vendor-neutral or well defined. They also cannot describe data much larger than 2^32 bits or blocks with different word sizes, and their checksums are too simple to detect errors well on large data.

SHF is meant to be simple enough for small tools to produce and parse, yet able to handle large and complex dumps and to detect errors using a standard cryptographic hash. It deliberately allows only hexadecimal notation and word sizes that are whole bytes. It is a dump format only, not a patch or configuration format that alters individual bits in a machine's memory.
sections.eli5: People had many different ways to write down the insides of a memory chip, and none were neat or safe for big files. SHF is one tidy way that works for small and huge jobs.

sections.title: Bytes, Words, Blocks and Dumps
sections.content:
The RFC defines four terms, and they are capitalized in the text.

  • Byte: a group of 8 bits. Octet is another name for it.
  • Word: a group of an integral number of Bytes.
  • Block: an ordered sequence of Words beginning at a certain address and running from lower to higher addresses.
  • Dump: a sequence of Blocks, in any order. A Dump might be a complete firmware image for an embedded system.

A Dump MUST contain at least one Block. A Block MUST contain at least one Word. The Word size MUST be at least one Byte, and each Block in a Dump MAY have its own Word size and start address.
sections.eli5: A word is one chunk of data, a block is a row of chunks that sit together, and a dump is a pile of blocks. Think of chunks as eggs, blocks as cartons and the dump as the whole delivery.

sections.title: The SHF XML Structure
sections.content:
An SHF file is an XML structure for one Dump. It has a dump element holding one or more block elements, and each Block is independent of the others. The data inside a block element is its hexadecimal Words.

The dump tag has two attributes. name is compulsory and is a string that identifies the Dump. blocks is optional and is the number of Blocks as a 64-bit hexadecimal value. It should be given whenever possible, and if present it should be verified, but a wrong value leads to implementation-defined behaviour.

The block tag has five compulsory attributes: name, start_address (the start address in Bytes), word_size (Bytes per Word), length (the number of Words inside the element) and checksum (the 20-Byte SHA-1 digest of the data). If length turns out to be untrue, the Block MUST be discarded. The total data size in bits is 8 * word_size * length, and that MUST NOT exceed (2^64)-1.

The checksum MUST be computed over the data the Block represents, not over its ASCII text. SHA-1 can only handle data up to (2^64)-1 bits, which is why that is the Block size limit.
sections.eli5: A dump is a labeled box, and each block inside has a sticker saying where it starts, how wide each piece is and how many pieces there are. A special code on the sticker lets you check that the contents are right.

sections.title: Rules and Limits
sections.content:
Every attribute that carries a value, and all of the data, MUST be in hexadecimal. Only the name attributes are free text. That way a reader is never unsure whether a number is in hex.

All values except the checksum MAY omit leading zeros, but the checksum MUST NOT. A Block's data and a single Word MUST each stay at or below (2^64)-1 bits. A consumer should make sure it can handle a Word length before it parses any Blocks, because failing to do so may cause buffer overflows and endanger the system running it.

Values and multi-byte Words MUST be big-endian, with the most significant hex digits on the left. The address value 1234 means 1234, not 3412. A producer or consumer on a little-endian machine has to swap bytes.

Whitespace has no meaning and exists only for readability. A parser should silently ignore any other non-hex characters that appear in these places. Since word size is counted in bytes, a block must contain an even number of hex digits, and malformed blocks should be ignored.
sections.eli5: Everyone writes numbers the same way, biggest digit first, using only the sixteen hex digits. Spaces are allowed just to make it easier to read.

sections.title: Three Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC gives three complete dumps. The first is a single one-byte-wide Block at address 0400 that holds a short ASCII message. The second is a 6502 machine-code program for calculating Fibonacci numbers, split into a Code Block at address 1000 and a Mem Block at address 1100.

The third shows wide data: a memory dump with a word_size of 5, so each Word is 40 bits wide, taken from a SMIL memory. It shows that Words need not be 8 or 16 bits. The examples also show that the numeric attributes are hex and can omit leading zeros, for instance length="e".
sections.eli5: The RFC shows three sample dumps, from a short message to a program to a memory with extra-wide pieces, so you can see how the labels look in practice.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
SHF only represents data. It does not guarantee that the data is genuine, harmless or free of malicious code. The per-Block SHA-1 digest checks that the data was transferred correctly; it is not a signature for the file as a whole.

If integrity for the whole file is needed, it has to come from something outside the SHF file, such as the XML signing mechanism in RFC 3275. The IANA registration adds that the decoded data may contain executable code for a target platform, so additional transport security may be applied, and certificates or checksums for such code can be included in hexdump form as a matter of implementation.
sections.eli5: SHF is like a list of what is in a package. It does not promise the package is safe, so if that matters you need a separate seal.

sections.title: Media Type and Extensions
sections.content:
The RFC registers the media type application/shf+xml. The charset parameter is required and MUST be UTF-8 in uppercase. The file extension is shf, and there is no single magic number at the start of a file. The type is a subset of XML 1.0, allowing only the five predefined entity references plus numeric ones. The XML and DOCTYPE declarations need not be present.

Section 10 allows extra attributes to be added, for example an execution start address on a Block or an address_space attribute for systems with several memories, as long as none are removed or redefined. The dump still counts as valid SHF, and parsers that do not know the new attributes silently ignore them.
sections.eli5: The RFC gives SHF its own file label so programs know what it is, and lets people add extra sticker fields as long as old readers can ignore them.

data.title: Symbolic example of an SHF Dump
data.code:
<dump name="(Human readable string)" blocks="(64-bit value)">
  <block name="(Human readable string)" start_address="(64-bit
         value)" word_size="(64-bit value)" length="(64-bit value)"
         checksum="(20-Byte digest)">
     (Data)
  </block>
</dump>
